anchors.statement_quote:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), and let geodesics
be the maximal geodesics with their affine parametrizations supplied by
[[thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map]] clause (a). Let $h$ be a smooth
positive definite metric on $M$ ([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]).

**(a)** For every compact $K\subseteq M$ there is a constant $c(K)\in[0,\infty)$
with the following property. Let $\gamma:J\to M$ be a nonconstant geodesic,
let $q>0$ be the $h$-speed of its affine velocity and let $\ell$ denote the
$h$-arclength parameter of $\gamma$, so that $q(\ell):=|d\gamma/d\lambda|_h$
is the $h$-norm of the affine velocity expressed in the parameter $\ell$. At
every parameter value with $\gamma(\ell)\in K$ one has
$$\left|\frac{d\log q}{d\ell}\right|\le c(K).$$

**(b)** Assume in addition that $(M,d_h)$ is complete and that every closed
$d_h$-bounded subset of $M$ is compact. Let $\gamma:(\alpha,\beta)\to M$ be a
maximal nonconstant geodesic with $\beta<+\infty$, let $\lambda_0\in(\alpha,\beta)$,
and let $K\subseteq M$ be compact with $\gamma([\lambda_0,\beta))\subseteq K$.
Suppose that the $h$-arclength of the tail is finite:
$$\int_{\lambda_0}^{\beta}\bigl|\gamma'(\lambda)\bigr|_h\,d\lambda<\infty .$$
Then the geodesic extends beyond $\beta$, contradicting the maximality of
$(\alpha,\beta)$; consequently no maximal geodesic can have a finite affine
endpoint while its tail remains in a compact set and has finite
$h$-arclength.

step_quotes.quote: 3.1 (The bound.) Let $K$ be compact. By [L2] there is $\kappa(K)<\infty$ with $|(\nabla_Z h)(X,Y)|\le\kappa(K)|X|_h|Y|_h|Z|_h$ for all points of $K$ and all tangent vectors there. On the parameters with $\gamma(\ell)\in K$: $|(\nabla_v h)(u,u)|\le\kappa(K)|u|_h^2|v|_h=\kappa(K)q^2$, so by step 2.1, $2q|q'|\le\kappa(K)q^2$, that is, $|d\log q/d\ell|\le\kappa(K)/2$ there. This proves (a) with $c(K):=\kappa(K)/2$. [step 2.1, L2, algebra]

anchors.statement_quote:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), and let geodesics
be the maximal geodesics with their affine parametrizations supplied by
[[thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map]] clause (a). Let $h$ be a smooth
positive definite metric on $M$ ([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]).

with the following property. Let $\gamma:J\to M$ be a nonconstant geodesic,
let $q>0$ be the $h$-speed of its affine velocity and let $\ell$ denote the
$h$-arclength parameter of $\gamma$, so that $q(\ell):=|d\gamma/d\lambda|_h$
is the $h$-norm of the affine velocity expressed in the parameter $\ell$. At
every parameter value with $\gamma(\ell)\in K$ one has
$$\left|\frac{d\log q}{d\ell}\right|\le c(K).$$

**(b)** Assume in addition that $(M,d_h)$ is complete and that every closed
$d_h$-bounded subset of $M$ is compact. Let $\gamma:(\alpha,\beta)\to M$ be a

step_quotes.quote:
1.1 (The rescaled velocity.) A nonconstant geodesic has no zero velocity at any parameter: a zero-velocity datum launches the constant solution, and ODE uniqueness would make the entire maximal solution constant. Therefore its $h$-speed is positive.  Let $\gamma:J	o M$ be a nonconstant geodesic with affine parameter $\lambda$ and let $\ell$ be $h$-arclength, so $d\ell/d\lambda=q>0$. Write $v:=d\gamma/d\ell$ for the $h$-unit velocity of $\gamma$ and $u:=d\gamma/d\lambda=q\,v$ for the affine velocity. Since $\gamma$ is a geodesic, $
abla_uu=0$, hence $
abla_vv=\sigma v$ for the function $\sigma:=-d\log q/d\ell$: indeed $
abla_{qv}(qv)=q^2
abla_vv+q\,v(q)\,v$, so $
abla_vv=- rac{v(q)}{q}v$ and $v(q)=dq/d\ell$ because $q$ is a function of $\ell$ along the curve. [given, L1, algebra]

4.1 (Bounds on the affine data up to the endpoint.) In the situation of clause (b), let $L:=\int_{\lambda_0}^{\beta}|\gamma'|_h\,d\lambda<\infty$ be the finite tail length and put $\ell(\lambda):=\int_{\lambda_0}^{\lambda}|\gamma'|_h\,dt$, a strictly increasing smooth map $[\lambda_0,\beta)\to[0,L)$ with smooth inverse, so $\ell\to L$ as $\lambda\to\beta$. By clause (a) applied on the tail, with $\gamma([\lambda_0,\beta))\subseteq K$, one has $q(\ell)\le q(0)e^{c(K)L}=:M$ and $q(\ell)\ge q(0)e^{-c(K)L}=:m>0$ for all $\ell\in[0,L)$. [given, step 3.1, algebra]

6.1 (Uniform ODE continuation.) Apply [L1] to the smooth first-order geodesic vector field in tangent-bundle charts. At every datum in $B$ it supplies a neighborhood of initial data and a positive common existence time in that chart. Take a finite subcover of $B$ by all such neighborhoods and let $\delta>0$ be smaller than their finitely many times. Every datum in $B$ therefore launches a geodesic for at least time $\delta$. Fix $\lambda_*\in(\lambda_0,\beta)$ with $\beta-\lambda_*<\delta/2$. The solution launched from $(\gamma(\lambda_*),\gamma'(\lambda_*))$ exists past $\beta$ and agrees with $\gamma$ on their overlap by uniqueness. Gluing it to the earlier part extends the affine geodesic beyond $\beta$, contradicting maximality and proving (b). This uses only a finite subcover and finite minima, so no choice principle is needed. [step 5.1, L1, contradiction] ∎

Statement: quantities that may vanish are treated explicitly or excluded by the stated positivity and nondegeneracy hypotheses; no step divides by a quantity that can be zero outside the stated exclusions.
Statement: the quantifiers range over all objects of the stated class, so the one-element and singleton instances are covered by the same argument; no step separates a cardinality-one case.

Statement: degeneracy is excluded by the standing hypotheses (nondegenerate Lorentzian metric, spacelike embedded hypersurface, embeddings with injective differential where used); no step proceeds through a degenerate configuration.

Statement and proof: the endpoint behaviour of the closed parameter intervals and of the boundary points of $U$ is handled explicitly where it occurs (limits of curves at the ends of their intervals, the closedness of $\partial U$); no completeness or extendibility beyond the stated domains is inferred.

anchors.statement_quote:
Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]) for the global causal structure and auxiliary-length calculus used below.

Let $(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ be a development of the given data
([[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]] clause (a)), write
$\Sigma:=j(\Sigma)$, and let $U_1,U_2\subseteq M$ be open with
$\Sigma\subseteq U_1\cap U_2$ such that $(U_i,g|_{U_i},N|_{U_i},j,\psi|_{U_i})$
is a development of the same data for $i=1,2$
([[def-gr-common-subdevelopment-and-corresponding-boundary]] clause (a), with
the identity as the embedding where it is defined; equivalently, both $U_i$
carry restricted development structures over the same initial embedding $j$).

anchors.statement_quote:
Throughout, for a smooth map $\psi:N\to N'$ between smooth Lorentzian
four-manifolds write $\psi^*(g')=g$ when $g_p(v,w)=g'_{\psi(p)}(d\psi_pv,d\psi_pw)$
for all $p\in N$ and $v,w\in T_pN$; such a map is an **isometric immersion**
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]]). Let $\nabla,\nabla'$ be
the metric-selected connections ([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]) and let geodesics
and exponential maps be those of
[[thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map]].

**(a) Rigidity.** Let $N$ be connected and let
$\psi_1,\psi_2:N\to N'$ be isometric immersions with
$\psi_1(p)=\psi_2(p)$ and $d\psi_1(p)=d\psi_2(p)$ for some $p\in N$. Then
$\psi_1=\psi_2$, that is, $\psi_1(q)=\psi_2(q)$ and $d\psi_1(q)=d\psi_2(q)$
for every $q\in N$.

**(b) Data-fixing embeddings have equal differentials on the initial surface.**
Let $(M,g,N,j,\psi)$, $(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ and $(U,g|_U,N|_U,j,\psi|_U)$ be
as in [[def-gr-common-subdevelopment-and-corresponding-boundary]] clause (a),
and let $\psi_1,\psi_2:U\to M'$ be development embeddings in the sense of
[[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]] clause (c). Then
$d\psi_1=d\psi_2$ at every point of $\Sigma:=j(\Sigma)\subseteq U$.

**(c) Agreement on overlaps.** Let $(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ and $(M',g',N',j',\psi')$
be developments of the same data, and let $(U_1,\psi_1)$ and $(U_2,\psi_2)$ be
common subdevelopments in the sense of
[[def-gr-common-subdevelopment-and-corresponding-boundary]] clause (a). Then
$\psi_1=\psi_2$ on $U_1\cap U_2$.

step_quotes.quote: 1.2 (The agreement set of (a).) Let $A:=\{q\in N:\psi_1(q)=\psi_2(q)\text{ and }d\psi_1(q)=d\psi_2(q)\}$. Then $p\in A$ by hypothesis, so $A\neq\emptyset$. [given, algebra]

1.5 (Every component of $U_1\cap U_2$ meets $\Sigma$.) Let $x\in U_1\cap U_2$. By [L4] $x$ lies in one of $I^-(\Sigma)$, $\Sigma$, $I^+(\Sigma)$; in the first two cases $x$ itself or a point of $\Sigma$ in the same component exists trivially; if $x\in I^+(\Sigma)$, choose a future timelike curve $\lambda$ in $M$ from a point of $\Sigma$ to $x$ ([L4]); by convexity of $U_1$ and of $U_2$ ([[lem-gr-subdevelopment-convexity]] clauses (a) and (c), applied to the causal curve $\lambda$ and to any subsegment with endpoints in $U_i$) $\lambda\subseteq U_1\cap U_2$, so $x$ lies in the same component of $U_1\cap U_2$ as a point of $\Sigma$; the case $x\in I^-(\Sigma)$ is the time reverse. [L4, algebra]
3.1 (Conclusion of (a).) $N$ is connected and $A$ is nonempty, open and closed by the preceding steps; hence $A=N$, which is the assertion of (a). [step 1.2, step 2.1, step 1.3, discharge-construct]

1.1 (The genuine pullback connection.) For an isometric immersion $\psi$ between these equal-dimensional nondegenerate manifolds, $d\psi$ is an isomorphism: its kernel is zero because $g(v,w)=g'(d\psi v,d\psi w)$ for all $w$. Thus $\psi$ is a local diffeomorphism. On each such neighborhood define $D_XY=(d\psi)^{-1}(
abla'_{\psi_*X}\psi_*Y)$. This pullback satisfies the affine-connection rules, including $D_X(fY)=X(f)Y+fD_XY$, and the local definitions agree on overlaps. Preservation of Lie brackets under a diffeomorphism gives zero torsion, and differentiating $g(Y,Z)=g'(\psi_*Y,\psi_*Z)\circ\psi$ gives metric compatibility. The unique torsion-free compatible connection is therefore $D=
abla$, by the metric-selected Levi-Civita theorem in [L1]. Hence $
abla'_{d\psi X}d\psi Y=d\psi(
abla_XY)$ locally and along curves; geodesics are mapped to geodesics with velocity $d\psi(\gamma')$. This does not treat a connection or the Koszul expression as tensorial in its second argument. [L1, algebra, construct]

Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ and $(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ be developments of the same data
in the sense of [[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]] clause (a),
with $\Sigma:=j(\Sigma)$. Then there exist $U^*\subseteq M$ and
$\psi^*:U^*\to M'$ such that:

**(a)** $(U^*,\psi^*)$ is a common subdevelopment of $M$ and $M'$ in the sense
of [[def-gr-common-subdevelopment-and-corresponding-boundary]] clause (a);

**(b)** for every common subdevelopment $(U,\varphi)$ of $M$ and $M'$ one has
$U\subseteq U^*$ and $\psi^*|_U=\varphi$; in particular $(U^*,\psi^*)$ is a
maximal common development in the sense of clause (b) of that definition, and
it contains $j(\Sigma)$;

**(c)** uniqueness: if $(U^\dagger,\psi^\dagger)$ also satisfies (a) and (b),
then $U^\dagger=U^*$ and $\psi^\dagger=\psi^*$.

Put $U^*:=\bigcup_{\alpha\in A}U_\alpha$, an open subset of $M$ containing $j(\Sigma)$; define $\psi^*:U^*\to M'$ by $\psi^*(p):=\psi_\alpha(p)$ for $p\in U_\alpha$. This is well defined by [L3]: if $p\in U_\alpha\cap U_\beta$, then $\psi_\alpha(p)=\psi_\beta(p)$. [L1, L3, construct]

in the sense of [[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]] clause (a),
with $\Sigma:=j(\Sigma)$. Then there exist $U^*\subseteq M$ and
$\psi^*:U^*\to M'$ such that:

**(a)** $(U^*,\psi^*)$ is a common subdevelopment of $M$ and $M'$ in the sense
of [[def-gr-common-subdevelopment-and-corresponding-boundary]] clause (a);

**(b)** for every common subdevelopment $(U,\varphi)$ of $M$ and $M'$ one has
$U\subseteq U^*$ and $\psi^*|_U=\varphi$; in particular $(U^*,\psi^*)$ is a
maximal common development in the sense of clause (b) of that definition, and
it contains $j(\Sigma)$;

**(c)** uniqueness: if $(U^\dagger,\psi^\dagger)$ also satisfies (a) and (b),
then $U^\dagger=U^*$ and $\psi^\dagger=\psi^*$.

step_quotes.quote: 2.1 ($U^*$ is a development with Cauchy surface $\Sigma$.) Let $\gamma:I\to U^*$ be a future causal curve inextendible in $U^*$, choose $t_0\in I$ with $\gamma(t_0)\in U_{\alpha_0}$, and let $J$ be the connected component of $\gamma^{-1}[U_{\alpha_0}]$ containing $t_0$. By [L4] the restriction $\gamma|_J$ is inextendible in $U_{\alpha_0}$ and therefore meets $\Sigma$ in exactly one parameter value of $J\subseteq I$; hence $\gamma$ meets $\Sigma$ at least once. If it met $\Sigma$ at two distinct parameter values, then by [L5] applied in $M$ this would contradict that $\Sigma$ is a Cauchy set of $M$; hence $\gamma$ meets $\Sigma$ in exactly one parameter value, and the same holds for past causal curves by the time reverse. Thus $(U^*,g|_{U^*},N|_{U^*},j,\psi|_{U^*})$ is a development of the same data: it is a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with $j(\Sigma)$ a spacelike embedded hypersurface (as $U^*$ is open in $M$), the field equations hold by [L6], the induced data are those of $j$ and $\psi$, and $\Sigma$ is Cauchy by the above. [step 1.1, L2, L4, L5, L6, algebra]

3.1 ($\psi^*$ is a data-fixing development embedding.) By [L2] each $\psi_\alpha$ is an isometric immersion fixing the data and the time orientation; these are local properties, so $\psi^*$ is a smooth isometric immersion with $\psi^*\circ j=j'$ and $g'_{\psi^*(p)}(d\psi^*_pN_p,N'_{\psi^*(p)})<0$ for every $p\in U^*$, matching every matter field by [L2]. Hence $\psi^*$ is a data-fixing isometric immersion of the development $U^*$ into $M'$; by [L6] it is injective and therefore a data-fixing development embedding. So $(U^*,\psi^*)$ is a common subdevelopment, which is clause (a). [step 2.1, L2, L6, algebra]

Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $(W,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and let $S\subseteq W$ be a closed acausal edgeless embedded topological hypersurface of codimension one. Here acausality forbids causal relations between distinct points of $S$ as in [[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]]; **edgeless** means that no $s\in S$ has the following property: every open neighborhood $U$ of $s$ admits $a\in I^-_U(s)$, $b\in I^+_U(s)$ and a timelike curve in $U$ from $a$ to $b$ avoiding $S$. All curves and inextendibility use [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]], so an inextendible end has no point limit in the specified ambient manifold. Define the ambient causal domains by
$$D^+(S)=\{p\in W:\text{every past-inextendible causal curve in }W\text{ through }p\text{ meets }S\},$$
$$D^-(S)=\{p\in W:\text{every future-inextendible causal curve in }W\text{ through }p\text{ meets }S\},\qquad D(S)=D^+(S)\cup D^-(S),$$
as in [[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]]. Then:

**(a)** $D(S)$ is open, contains $S$, and $D^\pm(S)\setminus S\subseteq I^\pm(S)$.

**(b)** Every causal curve in $W$ with endpoints in $D(S)$ lies in $D(S)$.

**(c)** Every causal curve in the induced open submanifold $D(S)$ which is inextendible there meets $S$ at exactly one parameter value. No smoothness or spacelikeness of the topological hypersurface is required.

step_quotes.quote: 4.1 If $q\in J^+(S)\setminus S$, take a causal curve $s\to q$ and a point $r$ on a sufficiently short initial segment. Step 3.1 puts $r$ above the graph. Its vertical predecessor $u\in S$ gives $u\ll r\le q$, hence $q\in I^+(S)$. Dually $J^-(S)\setminus S\subset I^-(S)$. For $p\in D^+(S)\setminus S$, the past half of the maximal timelike geodesic through $p$ is past-inextendible by [L3], and hence meets $S$; its timelike segment from that meeting to $p$ puts $p\in I^+(S)$. The dual argument proves the past-side inclusion. Also $S\subset D^+(S)\cap D^-(S)$ immediately. [step 3.1, L1, L3, given]

5.1 Let $s\in S$. If $s$ were not interior to $D(S)$, take $p_k\notin D(S)$ converging to $s$. At each $p_k$ choose a past-inextendible avoiding half and a future-inextendible avoiding half, concatenate them, and use step 1.2 to parametrize the two halves by signed arclength with $p_k$ at zero. Apply [L2] first to their past halves and then to the future halves of that subsequence. The two limits join at $s$ to an inextendible causal curve, and the common subsequence converges uniformly on each compact interval of the joined domain. Its short crossing segment through $s$ from step 3.1 forces the avoiding curves to meet $S$, contradiction. Thus $S\subset\operatorname{Int}D(S)$; together with step 4.2 and step 4.1 this proves (a). [step 3.1, step 1.2, step 4.2, A1, L2, L3, choose, contradiction]

step_quotes.quote: 1.2 We explain the arclength use in [L2]. For an avoiding one-sided causal curve, restrict to the half ending at the prescribed point. Its $h$-speed is locally integrable and positive almost everywhere, so its accumulated $h$-length is continuous strictly increasing. The inverse parameter gives a curve which is $1$-Lipschitz for $d_h$, because distance is at most original subcurve length; hence it is locally Lipschitz in charts. To verify the tangent and the arclength identity without assuming absolute continuity of the inverse parameter, let $\lambda(t)$ denote accumulated length. At almost every original parameter, both the chart curve and $\lambda$ are differentiable and $\lambda'(t)=\sqrt{h(\gamma'(t),\gamma'(t))}>0$. Their exceptional set has measure zero. An absolutely continuous real function sends a measure-zero set to a measure-zero set: cover that set by intervals of arbitrarily small total length and apply the defining AC modulus to bound the total lengths of their image intervals. Thus its image under $\lambda$ is null, locally and hence on a countable exhaustion. At each remaining new parameter $u=\lambda(t)$, the inverse difference quotient is $1/\lambda'(t)$, and the chain difference quotient of the reparametrized chart curve is $\gamma'(t)/\lambda'(t)$. It is nonzero future causal and has $h$-norm one. This proves both admissibility and $h$-arclength parametrization. If the available one-sided length were finite, the $1$-Lipschitz curve would be Cauchy at that end and completeness would give a point limit, contrary to inextendibility. Thus these reparametrizations have full half-line domains, as required by [L2]. This argument changes parameters and never asserts an extension preserving an arbitrary original parameter. [A1, L2, L3, given, construct]

3.1 A future causal segment starting at $s$ and remaining in this box cannot have an endpoint $q$ below the graph: the vertical segment from $q$ to the graph point $r$ gives $s\le q\ll r$, so $s\ll r$, excluded by step 1.1. If $q\in S$ and $q\ne s$, acausality excludes it. If $q=s$ but the segment is nondegenerate, choose an intermediate point $q'$ different from $s$ sufficiently near its start; it cannot lie below the graph or on $S$, so lies above it. Its vertical predecessor $r'\in S$ satisfies $r'\ll q'\le s$, again excluded by step 1.1. The same argument applies even if the rest of the loop leaves the box. Thus no nondegenerate causal loop passes through $S$, no causal curve meets $S$ twice, and every sufficiently short future segment from $S$ lies strictly above its local graph. Reversing time puts short past segments strictly below. Every causal curve through $s$ therefore crosses its local graph, and uniform approximations of a sufficiently short compact crossing segment also meet that graph by continuity of $t-f(z)$ and the intermediate value theorem. [step 1.1, step 2.1, L1, given]

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]), let $V\subseteq U\subseteq M$ be open
subsets with the induced metric and time orientation, and let
$\gamma:I\to U$ be a future causal curve
([[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]) that is inextendible in the
Lorentzian manifold $U$: $\gamma$ does not converge to any point of $U$ as its
parameter tends to either end of $I$ (clause (d) of
[[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]], read with ambient set $U$). Let $J$
be a connected component of
$$\gamma^{-1}[V]:=\{t\in I:\gamma(t)\in V\}.$$
Then $\gamma|_J$, regarded as a future causal curve in the Lorentzian manifold
$V$ with the restricted fields, is inextendible in $V$.

anchors.statement_quote:
Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let
$(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ and $(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ be developments of the same data
([[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]]), $(U,\varphi)$ a common
subdevelopment ([[def-gr-common-subdevelopment-and-corresponding-boundary]]
clause (a)), $\Sigma:=j(\Sigma)$, and let $p\in\partial U$ be an exposed
boundary point in the sense of [[lem-gr-boundary-null-geodesic-segment]]:
$$J^-(p)\cap\partial U\cap J^+(\Sigma)=\{p\}.$$
Fix a strictly convex normal neighbourhood $C$ of $p$
([[thm-gr-convex-normal-neighborhoods]]) with $C\subseteq I^+(\Sigma)$ and
$C\cap\partial U\subseteq C_{\mathrm{corr}}$, where $C_{\mathrm{corr}}$ is the
corresponding set of [[lem-gr-corresponding-set-smooth-extension]] (possible
because that set is open in $\partial U$ and $I^+(\Sigma)$ is open). Let
$p_1\ll p\ll p_2$ be points of $C$ such that $W:=I^+(p_1)\cap I^-(p_2)$
satisfies $\overline W\subseteq C$ (possible: strong causality at $p$ supplies
a neighbourhood $V_2\subseteq C$ of $p$ such that every causal curve with
both endpoints in $V_2$ is contained in $C$, and then
$\overline W\subseteq J^+(p_1)\cap J^-(p_2)\subseteq C$ for $p_1,p_2\in V_2$
by the same argument). Then $W$ is open, causally convex, $p\in W$, and
$\overline W$ is compact. Let $q\in W\cap I^+(p)$ be a point with
$$J^-(q)\cap U^c\cap J^+(\Sigma)\subseteq W,$$
chosen so close to $p$ along a future timelike curve that also $q\in W$
([[lem-gr-exposed-boundary-point]]). Let $\tau_q$ be the time separation from
$q$ ([[lem-gr-time-separation-maximizers]]) and put
$$K:=\overline W\cap U^c\cap J^+(\Sigma),\qquad \tau_0:=\max\{\tau_q(r):r\in K\}.$$
Let $W^\circ:=W\cap I^+(\Sigma)$ and let $S$ be the connected component of
the closed-in-$W^\circ$ set $\{x\in W^\circ:\tau_q(x)=\tau_0\}$ that contains
a maximizer of $\tau_q$ over $K$. Then:

**(a)** $\tau_0>0$; every maximizer of $\tau_q$ over $K$ lies in
$W\cap\partial U\cap C_{\mathrm{corr}}$; every $x\in W$ with
$\tau_q(x)>\tau_0$ lies in $U$; every $x\in W\cap U^c\cap J^+(\Sigma)$ with
$\tau_q(x)=\tau_0$ lies in $\partial U\cap C_{\mathrm{corr}}$.

**(b)** $S$ is a nonempty smooth embedded spacelike hypersurface of $M$
without boundary, subsets $S\subseteq(W\cap U)\cup(W\cap\partial U\cap
C_{\mathrm{corr}})$ and $S\cap\partial U\ne\varnothing$; moreover
$S\subseteq\{x:\tau_q(x)=\tau_0\}$ and every point of $S\cap U^c$ lies in
$\partial U\cap C_{\mathrm{corr}}$.

**(c)** There is a smooth positive function $\delta:S\to(0,\infty)$ with the
following properties. Define $X:=\nabla\tau_q/g(\nabla\tau_q,\nabla\tau_q)$
(so that $d\tau_q(X)=1$) on $\{\tau_q>0\}\cap W$, let $\phi_t$ be its local
flow, and put
$$F:S\times(-\delta,\delta)\to M,\qquad F(s,t):=\phi_t(s),\qquad N:=F\bigl(S\times(-\delta,\delta)\bigr).$$
Then $F$ is well defined and smooth, $N\subseteq W$ is open,
$F:S\times(-\delta,\delta)\to N$ is a diffeomorphism,
$\tau_q(F(s,t))=\tau_0+t$, and:

1. every causal curve in $N$ is, in the coordinates $(s,t)$, of the form
   $t\mapsto F(s(t),t)$ with $s(t)$ of finite length in the induced metric
   of $S$, and it meets $S$ in at most one parameter value;
2. every causal curve in $U\cup N$ that is inextendible in $U\cup N$ meets
   $U$, and consequently meets $\Sigma$ in exactly one parameter value; in
   particular no causal curve in $U\cup N$ that is inextendible in $U\cup N$
   and whose image is disjoint from $U$ exists;
3. for every $y\in N\cap U$ there is a unique $s\in S$ with $y=F(s,t_y)$, and the **punctured radial segment**
$$\{F(s,u):u\text{ between }0\text{ and }t_y,\ u\ne0\}$$
is contained in $U$. The base belongs to $U\cup C_{\mathrm{corr}}$, and the full segment including the base is contained in $U$ whenever $s\in U$. In particular, if $t_y<0$ then also $s\in U$. If $\Theta:N\to M'$ is a time-orientation-preserving local isometry with $\Theta|_S=\Phi|_S$, where $\Phi$ is the smooth extension of the common-subdevelopment map $\varphi$, then $\Theta=\varphi$ on $N\cap U$;
4. the tube can be chosen inside any prescribed open neighbourhood $O\subseteq W$ of the whole $S$, and below any prescribed positive continuous width ceiling on $S$. More quantitatively, write $q_0=g|_{TS}$ and $q_t=F_t^*g|_{TS}$. The construction gives $0<\delta<\tau_0/8$, $q_t\ge\tfrac12q_0$ for $|t|<\delta(s)$ and $|d\delta|_{q_0}\le1/(8\sqrt2)$. Every smooth positive smaller width $\widetilde\delta\le\delta$ satisfying $|d\widetilde\delta|_{q_0}\le1/(4\sqrt2)$ retains conclusions 1-3.

No compactness of $S$ or positive uniform lower bound for $\delta$ is assumed. The radial segment in clause 3 excludes its base because $S\cap\partial U\ne\varnothing$.

step_quotes.quote: 1.1 (Maximum and its boundary location.) The compact set $K$ is nonempty because it contains $p$; $\tau_q$ is finite and upper semicontinuous on $K$, so its maximum is attained and $\tau_0\ge\tau_q(p)>0$ by [L1]. A maximizer $r$ belongs to $I^-(q)\cap U^c\cap J^+(\Sigma)$, hence to $W$ by the assumed containment, and to $I^+(\Sigma)$ since $r\notin\Sigma\subset U$. If $r$ were interior to $U^c$, the timelike radial geodesic from $r$ to $q$ could be continued a little to the past within $W\cap\operatorname{int}(U^c)\cap I^+(\Sigma)$ by [L2]. the closed-in-$W^\circ$ set $\{x\in W^\circ:\tau_q(x)=\tau_0\}$ that contains
a maximizer of $\tau_q$ over $K$. Then:

**(a)** $\tau_0>0$; every maximizer of $\tau_q$ over $K$ lies in
$W\cap\partial U\cap C_{\mathrm{corr}}$; every $x\in W$ with
$\tau_q(x)>\tau_0$ lies in $U$; every $x\in W\cap U^c\cap J^+(\Sigma)$ with
$\tau_q(x)=\tau_0$ lies in $\partial U\cap C_{\mathrm{corr}}$.

without boundary, subsets $S\subseteq(W\cap U)\cup(W\cap\partial U\cap
C_{\mathrm{corr}})$ and $S\cap\partial U\ne\varnothing$; moreover
$S\subseteq\{x:\tau_q(x)=\tau_0\}$ and every point of $S\cap U^c$ lies in
$\partial U\cap C_{\mathrm{corr}}$.

(so that $d\tau_q(X)=1$) on $\{\tau_q>0\}\cap W$, let $\phi_t$ be its local

Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $(M,g,N)$ be a
globally hyperbolic time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-causal-conditions-and-global-hyperbolicity]] clause (c)), let
$L_g$ be the Lorentzian length functional on future causal curves
([[def-gr-timelike-worldline-and-proper-time]]), and for $q\in M$ define the
**time separation**
$$\tau_q:M\to[0,\infty),\qquad \tau_q(r):=\sup\{L_g(\alpha):\ \alpha \text{ is a future causal curve from } r \text{ to } q\},$$
the supremum over the empty set being $0$; thus $\tau_q(r)>0$ exactly for
$r\in I^-(q)$ and $\tau_q(r)=0$ for $r\notin J^-(q)$.

**(a)** For every $r\in J^-(q)$ one has $0\le\tau_q(r)<\infty$. If $r\ne q$, the supremum is attained by a future causal curve $\gamma$ from $r$ to $q$ with $L_g(\gamma)=\tau_q(r)$. Every such **nondegenerate maximizer** is, up to increasing reparametrization, a causal geodesic, with image in the compact set $J^+(r)\cap J^-(q)$. For $r=q$, $\tau_q(q)=0$ and the constant zero-velocity geodesic is the **degenerate maximizer** by convention. It has image $\{q\}$ and length zero; it is not asserted to belong to the curve class requiring nonzero causal velocity almost everywhere. This separates the reflexive case without changing the separation function or the nondegenerate maximizing claim.

**(b)** Let $V$ be a strictly convex normal neighbourhood of $q$ (as produced
by [[thm-gr-convex-normal-neighborhoods]]) and let $W\subseteq V$ be open and
causally convex in $M$ (every causal curve in $M$ with both endpoints in $W$
is contained in $W$), with $\overline W$ compact and $q\in W$. Then for every
$r\in W\cap I^-(q)$,
$$\tau_q(r)=\sqrt{-g_q\bigl(\exp_q^{-1}(r),\exp_q^{-1}(r)\bigr)},$$
so $\tau_q$ is smooth on $W\cap I^-(q)$ and extends continuously by
$\tau_q(q)=0$ and $\tau_q(r)=0$ for $r\in W\setminus J^-(q)$.

**(c)** On every compact set $K\subseteq M$ the function $\tau_q$ is upper
semicontinuous in the following strong form: for every sequence $r_n\to r$ in
$K$ one has $\limsup_n\tau_q(r_n)\le\tau_q(r)$. If moreover $r\in I^-(q)$,
then $\tau_q(r_n)\to\tau_q(r)$ for every sequence $r_n\to r$.

step_quotes.quote: 1.1 (Finiteness.) Let $r\in J^-(q)$ and let $\alpha$ be any future causal curve from $r$ to $q$. Every point of $\alpha$ lies in $J^+(r)\cap J^-(q)$, which is compact, so by [L1] the $h$-arclength of $\alpha$ and hence $L_g(\alpha)$ is bounded by a constant depending only on $r,q$; therefore $\tau_q(r)<\infty$. If $r\notin J^-(q)$ no such curve exists and $\tau_q(r)=0$; if $r=q$ causality excludes a nonconstant return curve and the stipulated zero-separation convention gives $\tau_q(q)=0$, represented by the constant degenerate geodesic as specified in (a); and $\tau_q(r)>0$ iff there is a future timelike curve from $r$ to $q$, i.e. $r\in I^-(q)$. [given, L1, algebra]

Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $(M,g,N)$ be a

([[def-gr-causal-conditions-and-global-hyperbolicity]] clause (c)), let

([[def-gr-timelike-worldline-and-proper-time]]), and for $q\in M$ define the

$r\in I^-(q)$ and $\tau_q(r)=0$ for $r\notin J^-(q)$.

Every such **nondegenerate maximizer** is, up to increasing reparametrization, a causal geodesic, with image in the compact set $J^+(r)\cap J^-(q)$. For $r=q$, $\tau_q(q)=0$ and the constant zero-velocity geodesic is the **degenerate maximizer** by convention. It has image $\{q\}$ and length zero; it is not asserted to belong to the curve class requiring nonzero causal velocity almost everywhere. $r\in W\cap I^-(q)$,

semicontinuous in the following strong form: for every sequence $r_n\to r$ in

Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Fix the data of
[[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]]: a smooth three-manifold
$\Sigma$ with smooth Riemannian metric $h$, smooth symmetric tensor $K$,
one fixed admissible covariant matter model with its complete smooth Cauchy
data $d$, and constants $\Lambda,\kappa$. The model and its complete data,
including all required initial derivatives and prescribed fields on empty
regions, are fixed throughout. Assume the supplied complete-data local
existence and geometric uniqueness hypotheses apply on every spacelike
restart surface occurring in comparisons, as required by that definition.
Assume that at least one development of these data exists.
Write $Z_0:=\Sigma\times\mathbb R$ and let $j_0:\Sigma\to Z_0$,
$j_0(x):=(x,0)$.

**(a) The set-sized family.** Let $\mathcal X$ be the collection of all
tuples $(U,g,N,\psi)$ such that $U\subseteq Z_0$ is an open neighbourhood of
$j_0(\Sigma)$ in $Z_0$, $g$ is a smooth Lorentzian metric on $U$, $N$ a time
orientation and $\psi$ matter fields of the sector on $U$, and
$(U,g,N,j_0,\psi)$ is a development of the data in the sense of
[[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]] clause (a). Then
$\mathcal X$ is a set, and it is nonempty provided at least one development
of the data exists.

**(b) Identifications.** For $\alpha=(U_\alpha,g_\alpha,N_\alpha,\psi_\alpha)$
and $\beta\in\mathcal X$ let $(U_{\alpha\beta},\varphi_{\alpha\beta})$ be
their maximal common development, regarded as a subset of $U_\alpha$
([[lem-gr-maximal-common-development]], [[def-gr-common-subdevelopment-and-corresponding-boundary]];
in the convention of the definition it is realised inside the first member).
Let $Z:=\bigsqcup_{\alpha\in\mathcal X}U_\alpha$ and let $\sim$ be the
equivalence relation on $Z$ **generated** by the relations
$x\sim\varphi_{\alpha\beta}(x)$ for $\alpha,\beta\in\mathcal X$ and
$x\in U_{\alpha\beta}$ (a finite chain of such steps, in either order).
Then the classes of two points $p\in U_\alpha$, $q\in U_\beta$ coincide if and
only if $p\in U_{\alpha\beta}$ and $q=\varphi_{\alpha\beta}(p)$.

**(c) The quotient.** Let $Q:=Z/{\sim}$ with quotient map $\pi$. Then
$\pi|_{U_\alpha}:U_\alpha\to Q$ is a homeomorphism onto an open subset
$Q_\alpha:=\pi(U_\alpha)$, the family $\{Q_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in\mathcal X}$
covers $Q$, and $Q$ is Hausdorff.

**(d) Structure.** $Q$ is a Hausdorff, second countable smooth four-manifold and carries a
unique smooth atlas (unique in the sense of maximal atlases compatible with
the charts below) making all maps $\pi|_{U_\alpha}$ diffeomorphisms onto open
subsets, together with a smooth Lorentzian metric $\bar g$, a time orientation
$\bar N$ and matter fields $\bar\psi$ such that every $\pi|_{U_\alpha}$ is an
isometry onto its image preserving time orientation and matter fields, and
such that $\bar j:=\pi|_{U_\alpha}\circ j_0$ (independent of $\alpha$) is a
common embedding of $\Sigma$ with induced data $(h,K,d)$. The field
equations hold on $Q$, and every causal curve in $Q$ that is inextendible in
$Q$ meets $\bar j(\Sigma)$ in exactly one parameter value. Consequently
$(Q,\bar g,\bar N,\bar j,\bar\psi)$ is a development of the data
in the sense of [[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]] clause (a).
The representative $\bar N$ is chosen to determine the common future cones;
it need not equal the pushforward of each representative $N_\alpha$.

**(e) Universality.** Every development $(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ of the same data
admits a data-fixing development embedding into $Q$ in the sense of
[[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]] clause (c).

step_quotes.quote: 1.1 (Clause (a).) Each member is determined by four subsets of fixed sets as in [L1], so separation makes $\mathcal X$ a set; it is nonempty whenever some development of the data exists, by transporting that development through the flow representation [L6] (this transport is carried out in the proof of clause (e) below and uses no new hypothesis). [L1, L6, algebra]

1.2 (Canonical representation of an arbitrary development.) Let $(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ be a development. By [L4] it is globally hyperbolic with Cauchy surface $j(\Sigma)$. Let $X,\Phi,T$ be as in [L6]. Each integral curve is defined on $\mathbb R$ and satisfies $T(\Phi(t,y))=T(y)+t$, so it has no endpoint in $M$ and meets $j(\Sigma)$ exactly once. The map $\chi:\Sigma\times\mathbb R\to M$, $\chi(x,t)=\Phi(t,j(x))$, is therefore bijective and smooth. At $(x,t)$ its differential sends tangent vectors from $\Sigma$ to $d\Phi_t(dj(T_x\Sigma))$ and the time direction to $X_{\Phi(t,j(x))}=d\Phi_t(X_{j(x)})$. Since $j(\Sigma)$ is spacelike, $X_{j(x)}$ is not tangent to it; since $\Phi_t$ is a diffeomorphism with inverse $\Phi_{-t}$, these images span $T_{\chi(x,t)}M$. Thus $\chi$ is a bijective local diffeomorphism, hence a diffeomorphism. Pulling back the metric, orientation representative and matter fields gives a tuple on $Z_0=\Sigma\times\mathbb R$ in $\mathcal X$, with $\chi\circ j_0=j$. This proves nonemptiness from the assumed development. The associated quotient embedding will be concluded after the quotient structure is established. [L6, L4, algebra]

The map $\chi:\Sigma\times\mathbb R\to M$, $\chi(x,t)=\Phi(t,j(x))$, is therefore bijective and smooth. At $(x,t)$ its differential sends tangent vectors from $\Sigma$ to $d\Phi_t(dj(T_x\Sigma))$ and the time direction to $X_{\Phi(t,j(x))}=d\Phi_t(X_{j(x)})$. Since $j(\Sigma)$ is spacelike, $X_{j(x)}$ is not tangent to it; since $\Phi_t$ is a diffeomorphism with inverse $\Phi_{-t}$, these images span $T_{\chi(x,t)}M$. Thus $\chi$ is a bijective local diffeomorphism, hence a diffeomorphism. Pulling back the metric, orientation representative and matter fields gives a tuple on $Z_0=\Sigma\times\mathbb R$ in $\mathcal X$, with $\chi\circ j_0=j$. This proves nonemptiness from the assumed development. The associated quotient embedding will be concluded after the quotient structure is established. [L6, L4, algebra]

5.1 (A countable dense set without assuming second countability of $Q$.) Choose a countable dense $D_0\subseteq S$. At every newly occurring point choose one tangent basis and retain it at all later stages; let $R_x$ be its rational span. Recursively set $D_{n+1}=D_n\cup\{\exp_xv:x\in D_n, v\in R_x, \bar g_x(v,v)<0, \exp_xv\text{ defined}\}$ and $D=\bigcup_nD_n$. These sets are countable by [L9], using the declared choice axioms for the recursion. To show density, take $p\in Q_\alpha$ and its member flow line from $z_0\in S$ to $p$ given by [L6]. If its flow parameter is zero, density of $D_0$ in $S$ suffices. Otherwise partition its compact segment into finitely many nonconstant timelike subsegments, each contained in a convex normal neighborhood within this member. Write their endpoints $z_0,\ldots,z_k=p$. For negative flow parameter the chords are past timelike; for positive parameter they are future timelike. We show inductively $z_i\in\overline{D\cap Q_\alpha}$: if $z_{i-1}$ has this property, choose $d\in D\cap Q_\alpha$ sufficiently near $z_{i-1}$. In the local two-point inverse the vector $v(d,z_i)$ is timelike by continuity and openness of the timelike set. Approximate it by a timelike $u\in R_d$ so closely that the member geodesic remains defined to time one and $\exp_du$ lies in any prescribed neighborhood of $z_i$ within $Q_\alpha$. Such $u$ exists by rational density and openness of the local exponential domain. If $d\in D_m$, then $\exp_du\in D_{m+1}\subseteq D$, with no claim that $m=i-1$. The exact inverse satisfies $\exp_d(v(d,z_i))=z_i$; no approximation error is added for this equality. This proves the induction and density of $D$ in $Q$. [step 4.1, L6, L8, L9, construct]

anchors.statement_quote:
Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Fix the data of
[[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]]: a smooth three-manifold
$\Sigma$ with smooth Riemannian metric $h$, smooth symmetric tensor $K$,
one fixed admissible covariant matter model with its complete smooth Cauchy
data $d$, and constants $\Lambda,\kappa$. The model and its complete data,
including all required initial derivatives and prescribed fields on empty
regions, are fixed throughout. Assume the supplied complete-data local
existence and geometric uniqueness hypotheses apply on every spacelike
restart surface occurring in comparisons, as required by that definition.
Assume that at least one development of these data exists.
Write $Z_0:=\Sigma\times\mathbb R$ and let $j_0:\Sigma\to Z_0$,
$j_0(x):=(x,0)$.

**(a) The set-sized family.** Let $\mathcal X$ be the collection of all
tuples $(U,g,N,\psi)$ such that $U\subseteq Z_0$ is an open neighbourhood of
$j_0(\Sigma)$ in $Z_0$, $g$ is a smooth Lorentzian metric on $U$, $N$ a time
orientation and $\psi$ matter fields of the sector on $U$, and
$(U,g,N,j_0,\psi)$ is a development of the data in the sense of
[[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]] clause (a). Then
$\mathcal X$ is a set, and it is nonempty provided at least one development
of the data exists.

**(b) Identifications.** For $\alpha=(U_\alpha,g_\alpha,N_\alpha,\psi_\alpha)$
and $\beta\in\mathcal X$ let $(U_{\alpha\beta},\varphi_{\alpha\beta})$ be
their maximal common development, regarded as a subset of $U_\alpha$
([[lem-gr-maximal-common-development]], [[def-gr-common-subdevelopment-and-corresponding-boundary]];
in the convention of the definition it is realised inside the first member).
Let $Z:=\bigsqcup_{\alpha\in\mathcal X}U_\alpha$ and let $\sim$ be the
equivalence relation on $Z$ **generated** by the relations
$x\sim\varphi_{\alpha\beta}(x)$ for $\alpha,\beta\in\mathcal X$ and
$x\in U_{\alpha\beta}$ (a finite chain of such steps, in either order).
Then the classes of two points $p\in U_\alpha$, $q\in U_\beta$ coincide if and
only if $p\in U_{\alpha\beta}$ and $q=\varphi_{\alpha\beta}(p)$.

**(c) The quotient.** Let $Q:=Z/{\sim}$ with quotient map $\pi$. Then
$\pi|_{U_\alpha}:U_\alpha\to Q$ is a homeomorphism onto an open subset
$Q_\alpha:=\pi(U_\alpha)$, the family $\{Q_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in\mathcal X}$
covers $Q$, and $Q$ is Hausdorff.

**(d) Structure.** $Q$ is a Hausdorff, second countable smooth four-manifold and carries a
unique smooth atlas (unique in the sense of maximal atlases compatible with
the charts below) making all maps $\pi|_{U_\alpha}$ diffeomorphisms onto open
subsets, together with a smooth Lorentzian metric $\bar g$, a time orientation
$\bar N$ and matter fields $\bar\psi$ such that every $\pi|_{U_\alpha}$ is an
isometry onto its image preserving time orientation and matter fields, and
such that $\bar j:=\pi|_{U_\alpha}\circ j_0$ (independent of $\alpha$) is a
common embedding of $\Sigma$ with induced data $(h,K,d)$. The field
equations hold on $Q$, and every causal curve in $Q$ that is inextendible in
$Q$ meets $\bar j(\Sigma)$ in exactly one parameter value. Consequently
$(Q,\bar g,\bar N,\bar j,\bar\psi)$ is a development of the data
in the sense of [[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]] clause (a).
The representative $\bar N$ is chosen to determine the common future cones;
it need not equal the pushforward of each representative $N_\alpha$.

**(e) Universality.** Every development $(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ of the same data
admits a data-fixing development embedding into $Q$ in the sense of
[[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]] clause (c).

step_quotes.quote: 2.1 (Clause (b): transitivity of the pairwise identifications.) The identity common development of a member with itself gives $U_{\alpha\alpha}=U_\alpha$ and $\varphi_{\alpha\alpha}=\operatorname{id}$ by maximality [L2]; reversing a common-development embedding gives the same identifications in the opposite order, by the same maximality. Let $p\in U_\alpha$, $q\in U_\beta$, $r\in U_\gamma$ with $p\sim q$ via $\varphi_{\alpha\beta}$ and $q\sim r$ via $\varphi_{\beta\gamma}$. Then $p\in U_{\alpha\beta}$ and $q=\varphi_{\alpha\beta}(p)\in U_{\beta\gamma}$, so $p\in V=\varphi_{\alpha\beta}^{-1}(U_{\beta\gamma})$, and by [L3] the pair $(V,\chi)$ is a common subdevelopment of $\alpha$ and $\gamma$ mapping $p$ to $\chi(p)=\varphi_{\beta\gamma}(\varphi_{\alpha\beta}(p))=r$. By the maximality property of the maximal common development of $\alpha$ and $\gamma$, $V\subseteq U_{\alpha\gamma}$ and $\varphi_{\alpha\gamma}(p)=\chi(p)=r$. Hence the identification of $p$ with $r$ holds at chain length two, and by induction at every finite chain length; the converse inclusion is the definition of the generating relations. This proves (b). [step 1.1, L3, algebra]

7.1 (A smooth global orientation representative.) The quotient is now a smooth manifold in the full sense of [L10]. Choose a subordinate locally finite smooth partition of unity $(\rho_\alpha)$ for the member cover and put $\bar N=\sum_\alpha\rho_\alpha(\pi|_{U_\alpha})_*N_\alpha$, extending each summand by zero outside $Q_\alpha$. Each summand is smooth because its support lies in $Q_\alpha$; the sum is locally finite. At every point the nonzero summands are positive multiples of vectors in the same future timelike component by step 4.1 and at least one coefficient is positive since the coefficients sum to one. Cone convexity makes $\bar N$ smooth, nowhere zero and future timelike. Every member map therefore preserves time orientation in the sense of preserving future cones. The metric and matter fields are the descended fields of step 4.1; the particular representative $\bar N$ is not claimed unique. [step 4.1, step 6.1, L10, construct]

9.1 (At most one Cauchy meeting.) Suppose a future causal curve $\gamma$ has two parameter values on $S$. In a member neighborhood of any meeting it can meet $S$ at most once, since $S$ is the member's acausal Cauchy surface. Thus its meeting parameters form a relatively closed locally discrete subset; on the compact interval between the proposed two meetings it is finite, and we may choose consecutive meetings $t_1<t_2$. The connected image $\gamma((t_1,t_2))$ misses $S$, so by step 8.2 it lies wholly in either $Q^-$ or $Q^+$. Near $t_1$ it lies in a member containing $\gamma(t_1)$, and the member side observation of step 8.2 puts it in $Q^+$. Near $t_2$ the same observation puts it in $Q^-$. This contradicts the disjointness of these sides. A past causal curve is treated by reversing its parameter. Together with step 8.1, every inextendible causal curve meets $S$ exactly once; all development conditions, including second countability, hold. [step 8.1, step 8.2, contradiction, algebra]

step_quotes.quote: 4.1 (The local smooth structure, fields and future cones.) Compose the charts of each member with $(\pi|_{U_\alpha})^{-1}$. On $Q_\alpha\cap Q_\beta=\pi(U_{\alpha\beta})$, the transitions use the smooth data-fixing diffeomorphism $\varphi_{\alpha\beta}$, so these charts generate a unique maximal compatible smooth atlas. The metrics and matter fields agree on overlaps and descend to $\bar g,\bar\psi$; the field equations hold locally. The pushforwards of $N_\alpha$ need not agree as vectors, but they select the same future timelike component on every overlap because $\varphi_{\alpha\beta}$ preserves future cones. Thus there is a consistent locally smooth choice of future cones, before any global representative field is asserted. The maps $\pi|_{U_\alpha}\circ j_0$ agree and define an embedded spacelike $S:=\bar j(\Sigma)$ with the prescribed induced data, since every member contains this entire surface and each member map is a diffeomorphism onto an open subset. 6.1 (An explicit countable basis.) In each fixed tangent basis at $d\in D$, let $B_d(a,r)$ denote a Euclidean ball with rational center $a\in\mathbb Q^4$ and rational radius $r>0$. Form the family of all $\exp_d(B_d(a,r))$ for which the ball lies in the exponential domain and $\exp_d$ restricts to a diffeomorphism onto an open subset of $Q$. This family is countable by [L9] and consists of open sets by its definition. Given $p\in O$ with $O$ open, choose a member containing $p$ and use its joint exponential inverse near $(p,p)$. For all $d$ in a sufficiently small open neighborhood of $p$ in that member, there is a velocity $v(d,p)$ inside an open fiber domain $H_d$ on which $\exp_d$ is a diffeomorphism onto an open set containing $p$. Choose such $d\in D$ by step 5.1. The open set $H_d\cap\exp_d^{-1}(O)$ contains $v(d,p)$, so a rational translated ball in the fixed basis at $d$ contains $v(d,p)$ and lies in this open set. Its image is a family member containing $p$ and contained in $O$. This proves the basis criterion and hence second countability of $Q$. [step 5.1, L8, L9, construct]

step_quotes.quote: 5.1 (A countable dense set without assuming second countability of $Q$.) Choose a countable dense $D_0\subseteq S$. At every newly occurring point choose one tangent basis and retain it at all later stages; let $R_x$ be its rational span. Recursively set $D_{n+1}=D_n\cup\{\exp_xv:x\in D_n, v\in R_x, \bar g_x(v,v)<0, \exp_xv\text{ defined}\}$ and $D=\bigcup_nD_n$. These sets are countable by [L9], using the declared choice axioms for the recursion. To show density, take $p\in Q_\alpha$ and its member flow line from $z_0\in S$ to $p$ given by [L6]. If its flow parameter is zero, density of $D_0$ in $S$ suffices. Otherwise partition its compact segment into finitely many nonconstant timelike subsegments, each contained in a convex normal neighborhood within this member. Write their endpoints $z_0,\ldots,z_k=p$. For negative flow parameter the chords are past timelike; for positive parameter they are future timelike. We show inductively $z_i\in\overline{D\cap Q_\alpha}$: if $z_{i-1}$ has this property, choose $d\in D\cap Q_\alpha$ sufficiently near $z_{i-1}$. In the local two-point inverse the vector $v(d,z_i)$ is timelike by continuity and openness of the timelike set. Approximate it by a timelike $u\in R_d$ so closely that the member geodesic remains defined to time one and $\exp_du$ lies in any prescribed neighborhood of $z_i$ within $Q_\alpha$. Such $u$ exists by rational density and openness of the local exponential domain. If $d\in D_m$, then $\exp_du\in D_{m+1}\subseteq D$, with no claim that $m=i-1$. The exact inverse satisfies $\exp_d(v(d,z_i))=z_i$; no approximation error is added for this equality. This proves the induction and density of $D$ in $Q$. [step 4.1, L6, L8, L9, construct]

7.1 (A smooth global orientation representative.) The quotient is now a smooth manifold in the full sense of [L10]. Each summand is smooth because its support lies in $Q_\alpha$; the sum is locally finite. At every point the nonzero summands are positive multiples of vectors in the same future timelike component by step 4.1 and at least one coefficient is positive since the coefficients sum to one. Cone convexity makes $\bar N$ smooth, nowhere zero and future timelike. Every member map therefore preserves time orientation in the sense of preserving future cones. The metric and matter fields are the descended fields of step 4.1; the particular representative $\bar N$ is not claimed unique. [step 4.1, step 6.1, L10, construct]

Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Fix the data of
[[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]]: a smooth three-manifold
$\Sigma$ with smooth Riemannian metric $h$, smooth symmetric tensor $K$,
one fixed admissible covariant matter model with its complete smooth Cauchy
data $d$, and constants $\Lambda,\kappa$. The model and its complete data,
including all required initial derivatives and prescribed fields on empty
regions, are fixed throughout. Assume the supplied complete-data local
existence and geometric uniqueness hypotheses apply on every spacelike
restart surface occurring in comparisons, as required by that definition.
Assume that at least one development of these data exists.
Write $Z_0:=\Sigma\times\mathbb R$ and let $j_0:\Sigma\to Z_0$,
$j_0(x):=(x,0)$.

**(a) The set-sized family.** Let $\mathcal X$ be the collection of all
tuples $(U,g,N,\psi)$ such that $U\subseteq Z_0$ is an open neighbourhood of
$j_0(\Sigma)$ in $Z_0$, $g$ is a smooth Lorentzian metric on $U$, $N$ a time
orientation and $\psi$ matter fields of the sector on $U$, and
$(U,g,N,j_0,\psi)$ is a development of the data in the sense of
[[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]] clause (a). Then
$\mathcal X$ is a set, and it is nonempty provided at least one development
of the data exists.

**(b) Identifications.** For $\alpha=(U_\alpha,g_\alpha,N_\alpha,\psi_\alpha)$
and $\beta\in\mathcal X$ let $(U_{\alpha\beta},\varphi_{\alpha\beta})$ be
their maximal common development, regarded as a subset of $U_\alpha$
([[lem-gr-maximal-common-development]], [[def-gr-common-subdevelopment-and-corresponding-boundary]];
in the convention of the definition it is realised inside the first member).
Let $Z:=\bigsqcup_{\alpha\in\mathcal X}U_\alpha$ and let $\sim$ be the
equivalence relation on $Z$ **generated** by the relations
$x\sim\varphi_{\alpha\beta}(x)$ for $\alpha,\beta\in\mathcal X$ and
$x\in U_{\alpha\beta}$ (a finite chain of such steps, in either order).
Then the classes of two points $p\in U_\alpha$, $q\in U_\beta$ coincide if and
only if $p\in U_{\alpha\beta}$ and $q=\varphi_{\alpha\beta}(p)$.

**(c) The quotient.** Let $Q:=Z/{\sim}$ with quotient map $\pi$. Then
$\pi|_{U_\alpha}:U_\alpha\to Q$ is a homeomorphism onto an open subset
$Q_\alpha:=\pi(U_\alpha)$, the family $\{Q_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in\mathcal X}$
covers $Q$, and $Q$ is Hausdorff.

**(d) Structure.** $Q$ is a Hausdorff, second countable smooth four-manifold and carries a
unique smooth atlas (unique in the sense of maximal atlases compatible with
the charts below) making all maps $\pi|_{U_\alpha}$ diffeomorphisms onto open
subsets, together with a smooth Lorentzian metric $\bar g$, a time orientation
$\bar N$ and matter fields $\bar\psi$ such that every $\pi|_{U_\alpha}$ is an
isometry onto its image preserving time orientation and matter fields, and
such that $\bar j:=\pi|_{U_\alpha}\circ j_0$ (independent of $\alpha$) is a
common embedding of $\Sigma$ with induced data $(h,K,d)$. The field
equations hold on $Q$, and every causal curve in $Q$ that is inextendible in
$Q$ meets $\bar j(\Sigma)$ in exactly one parameter value. Consequently
$(Q,\bar g,\bar N,\bar j,\bar\psi)$ is a development of the data
in the sense of [[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]] clause (a).
The representative $\bar N$ is chosen to determine the common future cones;
it need not equal the pushforward of each representative $N_\alpha$.

**(e) Universality.** Every development $(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ of the same data
admits a data-fixing development embedding into $Q$ in the sense of
[[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]] clause (c).

step_quotes.quote: 2.1 (Clause (b): transitivity of the pairwise identifications.) The identity common development of a member with itself gives $U_{\alpha\alpha}=U_\alpha$ and $\varphi_{\alpha\alpha}=\operatorname{id}$ by maximality [L2]; reversing a common-development embedding gives the same identifications in the opposite order, by the same maximality. Let $p\in U_\alpha$, $q\in U_\beta$, $r\in U_\gamma$ with $p\sim q$ via $\varphi_{\alpha\beta}$ and $q\sim r$ via $\varphi_{\beta\gamma}$. Then $p\in U_{\alpha\beta}$ and $q=\varphi_{\alpha\beta}(p)\in U_{\beta\gamma}$, so $p\in V=\varphi_{\alpha\beta}^{-1}(U_{\beta\gamma})$, and by [L3] the pair $(V,\chi)$ is a common subdevelopment of $\alpha$ and $\gamma$ mapping $p$ to $\chi(p)=\varphi_{\beta\gamma}(\varphi_{\alpha\beta}(p))=r$. By the maximality property of the maximal common development of $\alpha$ and $\gamma$, $V\subseteq U_{\alpha\gamma}$ and $\varphi_{\alpha\gamma}(p)=\chi(p)=r$. Hence the identification of $p$ with $r$ holds at chain length two, and by induction at every finite chain length; the converse inclusion is the definition of the generating relations. This proves (b). [step 1.1, L3, algebra]

Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]) for the mathematical suppliers.

Adopt the postulates [[post-gr-einstein-field-law]] (the Einstein field law
$G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa T_{ab}$ for a Lorentzian four-metric $g$ with
cosmological constant $\Lambda$ and coupling $\kappa$),
[[post-gr-spacetime-and-classical-domain]] (the classical smooth Lorentzian
domain, time orientation and the identification of $g$ as the gravitational
field), and [[post-gr-field-and-matter-assumptions]] (the selected matter
sectors, their equations of motion and stress-energy tensors, and the
requirement that the coupled system be treated within the stated
regularity).

Adopt the specified fixed matter equations and stress expression as model premises as well; for any additional model beyond the concrete sectors of the cited postulate, these are additional stipulated premises. Mathematical admissibility does not itself assert a physical matter law.

Let $\Sigma$ be a connected smooth three-manifold, let $h$ be a smooth
Riemannian metric and $K$ a smooth symmetric $2$-tensor on $\Sigma$, and let
complete smooth initial data for one fixed admissible coupled model of [[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]] be given, satisfying the constraints of [[thm-gr-constraint-equations-in-normal-frame]]. Assume its actual local existence and uniqueness/restart hypotheses, including complete matter initialization and recovery. The concrete branches of [[thm-gr-high-regularity-selected-matter-development]] include vacuum, scalar, strict fluid and nonnegative tilted geodesic dust with velocity through zero density; any further model must supply the same fixed-model obligations. Then, as a conditional deduction from the
adopted model:

**(a)** there exists a development
$(M_{\mathrm{max}},g_{\mathrm{max}},N_{\mathrm{max}},j_{\mathrm{max}},\psi_{\mathrm{max}})$
of these data in which $g_{\mathrm{max}}$ solves the adopted field law with
the adopted stress-energy tensor and the matter fields solve the adopted
matter equations, and which is maximal among developments of the same data
in the sense of [[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]] clause (d);

**(b)** every development of the same data admits a data-fixing development
embedding into $M_{\mathrm{max}}$, and any two maximal developments of the
same data are related by exactly one data-fixing isometry; thus within the
model the maximal development is determined by the initial data up to
isometry fixing the initial surface;

**(c)** $M_{\mathrm{max}}$ is globally hyperbolic with Cauchy surface
$j_{\mathrm{max}}(\Sigma)$, so the deduction yields a deterministic
initial-value formulation inside the model for those complete constrained data that also satisfy the stated admissibility and local/restart hypotheses.

The conclusion is a statement about the adopted model: it asserts that the
postulated equations, together with the mathematical hypotheses on the data
and the regularity requirements of the sector, imply the existence and
uniqueness of the maximal development as a conditional consequence. It makes
no assertion that the model or its data describe any observed system, and
carries no empirical content beyond the model premises.

step_quotes.quote: 1.1 (Relating the postulates to the mathematical model.) By [F1] and [F2] the field law and matter equations are those of the specified fixed model, with its complete data and actual admissibility/local uniqueness obligations; the four concrete sectors of [[thm-gr-high-regularity-selected-matter-development]] are included at their stated branch hypotheses. By [A1] the constraint equations are the model's compatibility conditions on the data. [F1, F2, A1, algebra]

2.1 (Existence of at least one development.) Under the hypotheses on the data the reduction hypotheses hold, so by [F3] the data admit at least one smooth development within the model's equations. [F3, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 (The maximal development exists and is unique.) Applying [F4] with step 2.1 as the nonemptiness input, the data have a maximal development $(M_{\mathrm{max}},g_{\mathrm{max}},N_{\mathrm{max}},j_{\mathrm{max}},\psi_{\mathrm{max}})$ which is unique up to a unique data-fixing isometry, and every development embeds into it. This is (a) and (b). [step 2.1, F4, algebra]

Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$,
$\kappa>0$, let $\Sigma$ be a connected smooth three-manifold with smooth
Riemannian metric $h$ and smooth symmetric $2$-tensor $K$, and let smooth
complete matter initial data be given for one fixed admissible covariant coupled model of [[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]], with the constraints satisfied and at least one development existing. The supplied local existence and uniqueness obligations must hold for that same model and for the complete data at every spacelike restart used in the proof. This includes vacuum, scalar, strict barotropic fluid and geodesic nonnegative tilted dust (with velocity prescribed through zero density) via [[thm-gr-high-regularity-selected-matter-development]]; additional fixed models must supply the same actual obligations. Then there exists a development
$(M_{\mathrm{max}},g_{\mathrm{max}},N_{\mathrm{max}},j_{\mathrm{max}},\psi_{\mathrm{max}})$
of the data in the sense of [[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]]
clause (a) that is maximal in the sense of clause (d) of that definition:
for every development $(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ of the same data there is a
data-fixing development embedding $M\to M_{\mathrm{max}}$. Moreover, if
$(M'_{\mathrm{max}},g'_{\mathrm{max}},N'_{\mathrm{max}},j'_{\mathrm{max}},\psi'_{\mathrm{max}})$
is another maximal development of the same data, then there is exactly one
data-fixing isometry $M_{\mathrm{max}}\to M'_{\mathrm{max}}$; the maximal
development is thus unique up to a unique data-fixing isometry. It is
connected and, by [[thm-gr-cauchy-surface-implies-globally-hyperbolic]],
globally hyperbolic with Cauchy surface $j_{\mathrm{max}}(\Sigma)$.

step_quotes.quote: 1.1 (Existence.) Let $Q$ be the quotient of [[lem-gr-universal-development]]. By [L1] it is Hausdorff and locally Euclidean with a smooth atlas, metric, time orientation and matter fields; by [L2] it is second countable; by [L1] its initial surface is met exactly once by every inextendible causal curve and the field equations and induced data hold. Hence by [L6] $Q$ is a development of the data. [L1, L2, L6, algebra]

step_quotes.quote: 2.1 (Uniqueness.) Let $Q,Q'$ both be maximal developments of the data. By maximality of $Q'$ applied to the development $Q$, there is a data-fixing development embedding $\Phi:Q\to Q'$; by maximality of $Q$ applied to $Q'$, there is $\Phi':Q'\to Q$. The composition $\Phi'\circ\Phi:Q\to Q$ is a data-fixing isometric immersion of the development $Q$ into itself (compositions of isometric immersions preserving the data and the time orientation are again such); by [L4] it is the identity of $Q$ because $Q$ is connected by [L5]. Similarly $\Phi\circ\Phi'=\mathrm{id}_{Q'}$. Hence $\Phi$ is a data-fixing isometry with inverse $\Phi'$, and $Q,Q'$ are isometric over the data. [step 1.2, L4, L5, algebra]

3.1 (Uniqueness of the isometry.) If $\Phi_1,\Phi_2:Q\to Q'$ are both data-fixing isometries, then on the connected development $Q$ the two data-fixing isometric immersions coincide by [L4]; hence the isometry is unique. [step 2.1, L4, algebra]

step_quotes.quote: 1.1 (Existence.) Let $Q$ be the quotient of [[lem-gr-universal-development]]. By [L1] it is Hausdorff and locally Euclidean with a smooth atlas, metric, time orientation and matter fields; by [L2] it is second countable; by [L1] its initial surface is met exactly once by every inextendible causal curve and the field equations and induced data hold. Hence by [L6] $Q$ is a development of the data. [L1, L2, L6, algebra]

2.1 (Uniqueness.) Let $Q,Q'$ both be maximal developments of the data. By maximality of $Q'$ applied to the development $Q$, there is a data-fixing development embedding $\Phi:Q\to Q'$; by maximality of $Q$ applied to $Q'$, there is $\Phi':Q'\to Q$. The composition $\Phi'\circ\Phi:Q\to Q$ is a data-fixing isometric immersion of the development $Q$ into itself (compositions of isometric immersions preserving the data and the time orientation are again such); by [L4] it is the identity of $Q$ because $Q$ is connected by [L5]. Similarly $\Phi\circ\Phi'=\mathrm{id}_{Q'}$. Hence $\Phi$ is a data-fixing isometry with inverse $\Phi'$, and $Q,Q'$ are isometric over the data. [step 1.2, L4, L5, algebra]
